title: AIE photosensitizer-integrated electrospun cellulose acetate nanofibers for photodynamic antibacterial wound repair
content: Bacterial infection can severely impair wound healing by sustaining inflammation and disrupting tissue regeneration, motivating the development of non-antibiotic biomaterials that combine effective antibacterial activity with favorable wound-healing properties. Here, we incorporate the aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizer DTPA-BT-F into cellulose acetate (CA) nanofibers through electrospinning to create a photodynamic dressing activated by visible light. Upon illumination, DTPA-BT-F efficiently produces reactive oxygen species (ROS) through Type I and Type II pathways, providing strong antibacterial effects against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli while retaining favorable cytocompatibility. Incorporation of DTPA-BT-F into the CA matrix preserves the uniform nanofibrous architecture and produces a flexible membrane with suitable mechanical properties, surface wettability, and water vapor permeability for wound-dressing applications. In a full-thickness S. aureus-infected wound model, the CA@DTPA-BT-F membrane markedly accelerates wound closure and promotes epidermal regeneration and collagen deposition. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses further reveal reduced inflammatory responses and enhanced angiogenesis, accompanied by no obvious systemic toxicity. These results demonstrate that coupling AIE-mediated dual-pathway photodynamic activity with an electrospun fibrous biomaterial provides an effective strategy for constructing antibacterial wound dressings and offers a promising platform for infected wound repair.
